confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Downloaded: 6,003,314 bytes, 48 pages, 72,025 extractable characters. Idamalayar: 168.06 m on 8 Aug, about 97% live storage full, peak inflow 1164 cumec on 16 Aug, average spill 1271 cumec, no attenuation. Neeleswaram: 'maximum discharge ... 8800 cumec on 16 August 2018' at EL 12.4 m (earlier HFL 11.105 m on 27 July 1974), and 'apart from a release of about 1500 cumec from Idukki reservoir, the flood peak generated in the downstream free catchment was of the order of about 7300 cumec'. confirmed_sources.name: CEA (Cyber Security in Power Sector) Guidelines, 2021 — authoritative CEA copy
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: I REPLACED the previously reported aegcl.co.in mirror with this CEA-hosted original and proved they are the same file (both md5 40498ff8ccad5a6d56a020018a1a84d8, 567,765 bytes). 24 pages, 55,202 extractable characters. VERIFIED in the text: applicability to 'Load despatch centres (State, Regional and National), Generation utilities (Hydro, Thermal, Nuclear, RE), Distribution Utilities, Generation Aggregators, Trading Exchanges, Regional Power Committees, and Regulatory Commissions', extended to 'System Integrators, Equipment Manufacturers, Suppliers/Vendors, Service Providers, IT Hardware and Software OEMs engaged in the Indian Power Supply System'. IEC 62443 listed as 'Cyber Security for Industrial Control Systems' alongside IEC 61850, IEC 62351 and IS 16335. Cardinal principle, verbatim: 'There is hard isolation of their OT Systems from any internet facing IT system', at most one internet-facing IT system per site isolated from all OT zones under CISO control, with data movement only via a whitelisted device and logs retained by the CISO for at least 6 months. Article 8 requires 'an annual cyber security training program for personnel having authorized cyber or authorized physical access ... to their Critical Systems', and the Information Security Division must be manned by engineers certified by 'Training Institutes designated by CEA'. RTU/PLC conformance to IEC 60870-5-101/104 with IEC 62351 security extensions.
confirmed_sources.relevance: The actual quotable basis for a read-only architecture. The 'hard isolation of OT from any internet-facing IT system' cardinal principle is a far stronger argument for a one-way/diode design than the audit-cadence claim it replaces.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: partly — applicability, IEC 62443, OT asset and perimeter identification, CEA-designated training and the SCADA/PLC/RTU scope are all confirmed; but the claimed 'IT systems audited at least every SIX MONTHS and OT systems at least ANNUALLY' does NOT appear anywhere in the document, and 'training within 90 days of notification' is a misreading — the document's 90 days is a cyber-log and forensic-record retention period, and its six months is CISO log custody plus an Alternate CISO skills deadline

confirmed_sources.name: CWC Advisory Flood Forecast (AFF) — methodology
confirmed_sources.what_it_provides: Fetched and confirmed on every point: 'CWC is currently doing rainfall-based mathematical modelling for flood forecasting which uses both the hydrologic (rainfall-runoff) and hydrodynamic modelling technique for real-time water level and inflow prediction'; 'Currently there are 20 river basin models running in the background covering the entire Flood Forecasting network'; 'These models run every three hours, day and night'; 'The 7 day advance forecast generated is derived from various available rainfall data products'. Inputs listed: satellite rainfall, rain-gauge data, IMD GFS and WRF forecast rainfall, river cross-sections, historical discharge and water level, and bathymetry. The workflow is described as fully automatic with 'no human intervention'.
confirmed_sources.relevance: The most direct answer to GAP 3. A 7-day, 3-hourly national inflow-forecast product built on exactly the input stack AquaSync would need is the realistic replacement for perfect-foresight optimisation — replace the oracle with an AFF-style ensemble and re-run the policy search.
confirmed_sources.content_matches_claim: yes — 3-hourly cadence, 7-day lead, 20 basin models, the hydrologic plus hydrodynamic coupling and every listed input all confirmed

The form works as a POST to https://sldckerala.com/index.php?id=7 with body date1=YYYY-MM%2FDD-YY&date1_dp=1&date1_day=DD&date1_month=MM&date1_year=YYYY&sbtstore=SHOW (note the odd YYYY-MM/DD-YY date1 format with a 2-digit year suffix; GET does not work and txtDate=<epoch> does not work, which is why the earlier attempt failed). I confirmed distinct real data at 2019-08-08, 2019-08-15, 2019-09-01, 2020-01-01, 2020-04-01, 2020-06-01, 2020-08-13, 2020-09-25, 2020-10-15, 2021-03-15, 2021-04-30, 2021-10-20, 2025-10-15 and 2026-08-25. The archive begins in early August 2019 (2019-08-05 empty, 2019-08-08 populated) and does NOT reach 2018. This gives AquaSync a daily observed-inflow-and-spill series covering the whole corrupt 2020-09-25 to 2021-04-30 window plus a year before the amith-vp dataset starts — and at 2021-10-20 it returns Idukki level 730.959 m with spill 9.072 and inflow 29.793 mcm/day, an independent cross-check on the flagship October 2021 case study that the GitHub dataset cannot provide.

THE ALERT-BAND FINDING IS BETTER THAN CLAIMED AND NOW HAS AN EXACT RULE. The earlier report said the bands 'MOVE with the rule curve through the monsoon' based on comparing a July workbook against an August dashboard. I read four sheets inside the single July-2026 workbook and the bands move WITHIN the month: rule 2375.33 ft on 01.07 and 10.07, 2377.95 on 20.07, 2380.58 on 31.07. More usefully, the offsets are exactly constant — Blue = rule minus 8.00 ft, Orange = rule minus 2.00 ft, Red = rule minus 1.00 ft for Idukki (and rule minus 1.5 / 1.0 / 0.5 m for Idamalayar). The August dashboard values 2389.78/2395.78/2396.78 obey the same offsets, implying rule 2397.78. So the policy search can implement the constraint as one rule-curve time series plus three fixed offsets rather than scraping three columns.

THE THREE OFFICIAL KERALA SOURCES DISAGREE WITH EACH OTHER ON THE SAME DATE. For 25/08/2026: the KSDMA daily KSEB bulletin gives Idukki water level 2364.22 ft with rule level 2390.09 ft and bands 2382.09/2388.09/2389.09; the KSEB dashboard gives 720.968 m (about 2365.38 ft) with bands 2389.78/2395.78/2396.78 (implied rule 2397.78); SLDC gives 720.968 m with remarks 2365.38 ft. SLDC and the dashboard agree on level, the KSDMA bulletin does not, and the two published alert-band sets differ by about 7.7 ft. This is a genuine reconciliation problem AquaSync must handle before treating any of them as a hard constraint — it is not a transcription error on anyone's part.

THE 2018 RECOVERY IS REAL BUT MUST BE STATED PRECISELY, AND THE FLOOD PEAK IS NOT IN IT. My independent parse reproduced the 104-row count exactly (Jun 31, Jul 32, Aug 10, Sep 9, Oct 22) and confirmed Nov/Dec 2019 dropped the column. But 104 rows collapse to only 96 unique 2018 dates, and only THREE of them are in August 2018 — the 20th, 30th and 31st. The 9-17 August 2018 flood peak, the whole reason anyone wants 2018 data, is absent from the KSEB workbooks. The earlier report said this honestly; keep saying it. Separately, the '25.09.2018 Sheet1 (2)' bonus sheet was attributed to the August-2019 workbook — it is actually present identically in the June, July AND August 2019 workbooks, so de-duplicate on it.

THE KSEB ARCHIVE IS 86 FILES, NOT 91, AND CHANGES FILE FORMAT MID-STREAM. 91 wpdmdl IDs are listed but IDs 310-314 (Jan-May 2019) 302-redirect to a dead kseboa.in host. Working range is 315 (June 2019) through 6380 (July 2026). Also, ID 1178 (Nov 2020) onward are legacy .xls, not .xlsx — openpyxl will refuse them, so a loader needs xlrd or a conversion step. This matters because the .xls stretch is exactly the corrupt-window months (Nov 2020 to Apr 2021) that AquaSync most wants to recover.

TWO CEA COMPLIANCE NUMBERS IN THE EARLIER REPORT ARE NOT IN THE CEA DOCUMENT. The '6-month IT audit / annual OT audit' cadence and the 'training within 90 days of notification' deadline do not appear in the 55,202 characters of the CEA Guidelines 2021. The real quotable provisions are stronger for AquaSync's purposes anyway: the cardinal principle 'There is hard isolation of their OT Systems from any internet facing IT system', at most one internet-facing IT system per site under CISO control with whitelisted-device-only data movement, Article 8's annual training programme, and CEA-designated Training Institutes for ISD engineers. Rebuild the read-only-architecture argument on those. I also replaced the aegcl.co.in mirror with the CEA-hosted original and proved md5 equality.

THE GOVERNANCE TRIGGER HAD NO URL AND NOW DOES. G.O.(Rt) No. 453/2021/DMD was presented as a key finding with no source at all — precisely the failure mode the brief warns about. I located and verified it at https://sdma.kerala.gov.in/dam-management/ (200), where the text appears verbatim including 'The committee meets when dams reach their orange level of alert or if extreme rainfall events are forecasted in the catchments of the State.' The same page indexes EAPs for 19 KSEB and 15 Irrigation dams. Honest limit: of the 19 KSEB rows only Kallarkutty carries a link, the Idukki-Cheruthoni EAP cell is EMPTY, and the page's only kseb.in href is dead (curl 000). Kerala's rule curves are referenced as existing and approved but are not published here — obtaining the Idukki rule curve is a request, not a download.

THE CWC 8-HOUR TRAVEL TIME IS REAL BUT IS A 2018-ONLY WORKING ASSUMPTION, NOT A CALIBRATED LAG. Verified verbatim in sec 8.3.2.2. But read the full sentence: the analysis 'was done only for 2018 using the outflow hydrograph from calibrated Mike-11 model at Idukki and Idamalayar dams' because 'hourly discharge from these project authorities were not available'. So the 8 h was derived against MODELLED dam outflow, not gauged releases, over a single event, because Idukki has spilled only three times ever (1988, 1992, 2018 — also verified verbatim). It is a legitimate government-published prior for Muskingum K and far better than a pure geometry estimate, but it is not gauge calibration: GAP 2 is narrowed, not closed. The same section also contradicts itself on the intervening free catchment area (2,329 km2 then 3,042 km2).

THE SEPT-2018 CWC REPORT IS NARRATIVE PLUS CHARTS, NOT A DOWNLOADABLE HOURLY SERIES. Every one of the 26 numbers I checked is verbatim in the text — 2532 cumec at 22:00 on 15 Aug, 41% attenuation, FRL touched 01:00 on 17 Aug, Idamalayar 168.06 m / 1164 cumec / 1271 cumec average spill, Neeleswaram 8800 cumec at EL 12.4 m with about 7300 cumec from the free catchment, Periyar 4,033 km2, free catchments 605 and 472 km2, Idukki 1997/537/1460 MCM. But Fig.4 is a chart image; the extractable text gives roughly ten dated waypoints, not a digitisable hourly series. Do not promise hourly 2018 Idukki data from this PDF without a chart-digitisation step. The report is also internally inconsistent on Periyar area (4,033 vs 4,035 vs 4,076 km2 across three tables).

UNDER-REPORTED VALUE WORTH PROMOTING, AND ONE SOURCE DEMOTED. Three things the earlier sweep found but undersold: (1) the KSEB daily sheets carry Power House Discharge, Spill (MCM) and Average Inflow (Cumec) columns omitted from the schema description — observed release partitioning, directly useful for calibrating the hydropower and spill models; (2) the CWC Dec-2018 report contains 2/5/25/50/100-year return-period inundation maps, a '100 Year vs 2018 Inundation Map', 'Flood Vulnerable Areas' and Figure 20 'Hotspots in ALWAYE' — published inundation hotspots for Aluva itself, a real starting point for GAP 4 — plus sec 8.5 'Flood Control Levels at Important Reservoirs' and sec 8.6 'Integrated Reservoir Operation'; (3) NDSA Reg 10 (seismological station data, s.34(1)) and especially Reg 11 (location and manner of collection, compliance, process and storage of data, s.34(2)) were missed and are directly on-point for a telemetry and storage layer. Demoted: pymodbus is a real, healthy repo but I moved it to 'rejected' because listing it implies a field-bus integration path that no evidence supports.
